findings.text: Virtual machine lifetime uses reference counting where safe acquisition succeeds only while a prior reference remains and release triggers full teardown when the final reference disappears.

Memory slot collections are accessed per address space through helpers that bound the identifier, dereference under sleepable read protection, report how many spaces exist, and iterate entries while treating empty slots as skipped warnings.
Large page coverage for a slot at a requested paging level is derived from the slot base and length by converting the final guest frame to an index and adding one.

Input output bus membership can be shrunk by removing one device, rebuilding a shorter bus image, publishing it, waiting for readers, then invoking optional per device cleanup and freeing old storage.
Opening the reverse map statistics file first pins the virtual machine, then attaches a single show routine, releasing the pin if attachment fails and reporting absence when pinning is impossible.

Virtual machine destruction proceeds through notifier and list removal, architecture pre cleanup, bus and coalesced resource release, memory notifier detachment with invalidation balancing, architecture and device teardown, per space slot freeing, sleepable read cleanup, and final virtualization disable and memory release.

Architecture teardown clears private mappings only when caller context matches virtual machine memory, then releases performance mediation, virtual processors, filters, interrupt controllers, address maps, memory management structures, tracking, and vendor extensions.
Reverse map head encodes emptiness as zero, single mapping as a value without the many flag, and multiple mappings as a flagged pointer to a descriptor whose two counters sum to the total.
Shadow page address space identity is determined solely by the system management role flag, selecting one of two spaces.
Shadow entry to frame conversion masks and shifts the entry, while child table lookup yields a pointer only for present non terminal entries and null otherwise.
A frozen entry is recognized by equality with a dedicated sentinel, and mirror status is inherited from the owning shadow page role through the entry container.

Changes between shadow entries forbid direct replacement of one present terminal mapping with another covering a different frame, tolerate identical rewrites, and restrict transitions between absent values to input output or frozen cases with tracing.
Writable state must remain consistent across memory management, host, and architectural views, with violations reported as one time warnings naming the offending entry.

Invalidated two dimensional paging roots are reclaimed by marking valid roots invalid, then under appropriate locking clearing scheduled flags, requiring invalid role, zapping each root in passes from fine to coarse granularity, and dropping the root reference.

Shared updates to two dimensional entries freeze mirror locations before applying external effects and unfreeze to the desired or restored value afterward, while non mirror failures are treated as fatal virtual machine errors and all stores use single write semantics with validation.
Slot and bus lookup require holding the slots mutex or equivalent protection, with publication through read copy update and reclamation delayed until sleepable readers finish.

Device unregistration and private region clearing acquire the slots mutex around bus mutation, while interrupt controller teardown additionally synchronizes pending delayed work before taking the lock.

Two dimensional root reclamation holds the memory management lock in shared mode for concurrent paths and exclusive mode otherwise, with iteration helpers asserting the hold and verifying read versus write ownership from a flag.
Root zapping and atomic entry updates execute under read side protection for table walk safety, and stores to entries go through read copy update dereference.

Per virtual machine memory caches hold objects from either slab or page allocation, are drained individually until empty, then have backing storage released and capacity reset, with three split caches cleaned during memory management teardown plus hash table release.

Hypervisor enlightenment state keeps an identifier indexed collection of event contexts released individually on teardown, while interrupt controller pointers in architecture state are cleared after device removal and memory release.
Hypervisor teardown has both a substantive implementation that walks and destroys the connection map and a configuration dependent empty form that performs no action.
Replacing a present terminal entry with another present terminal entry for a different frame is treated as host fatal to avoid guest data corruption, preceded by diagnostic logging.

If memory management notifier unregistration strands an active invalidation, the counter is forcibly cleared with warnings about unbalanced state or lingering progress flags to avoid deadlock during slot release.
Failure to allocate a shrunken bus image causes complete bus removal with an error log and negative memory error return, destroying all attached devices rather than only the target.

Zapping requires an elevated root reference so memory management notifier paths can observe the root while locks are dropped, and no explicit translation flush is issued because reuse and migration paths already flush locally.
The implementation exposes a named limit for how many memory slot address spaces a virtual machine may carry.
Virtual machine teardown iterates a fixed count of input output buses and emits a destruction notification event.
Device attachment distinguishes programmatic input output and memory mapped buses through dedicated enumerants.
Two dimensional reclamation names distinct paging granularities from small page through large sizes up to root level, plus dedicated absent and frozen entry encodings.
